title: Saying Sorry
goal: Acknowledge your own mistake, respond to an apology, and distinguish an apology from sympathy or a request for repetition.

runs.text: Sorry
can acknowledge a small accident.
I'm sorry
can begin a fuller apology. Naming the action helps the other person know what you are taking responsibility for.
Sorry I stepped on your foot.
Acknowledge the accident.
I'm sorry I kept you waiting.
Acknowledge the delay.
That was my mistake.
Take responsibility.
I should have told you sooner.
Recognize what you failed to do.
I'll send the correct file now.
Offer a concrete next step.
A missed message

turns.speaker: Cam

runs.text: You said you'd send me the address. I waited outside.

turns.en: You said you'd send me the address. I waited outside.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: I'm sorry. I forgot to send it. That was my mistake.

turns.en: I'm sorry. I forgot to send it. That was my mistake.

turns.speaker: Cam

runs.text: Thanks for saying that. Please send it before I leave next time.

turns.en: Thanks for saying that. Please send it before I leave next time.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: I will. Here's the address now.

turns.en: I will. Here's the address now.

runs.text: The explanation identifies the problem; it does not erase the effect. A next step is useful when there is something to fix. You do not have to make a promise you cannot keep.
My bad
is an informal acknowledgment that a mistake was yours.
Oops, sorry
can respond to an immediate small accident.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: You put the wrong time in the message.

turns.en: You put the wrong time in the message.

turns.speaker: Cam

runs.text: My bad. It should say seven, not six. I'll correct it.

turns.en: My bad. It should say seven, not six. I'll correct it.

blocks.caption: Informal responsibility and stronger apologies · Jules & Cam

runs.text: Here the informal wording accompanies a specific correction. If the other person is seriously hurt or the problem remains unresolved, a brief
My bad
alone may not communicate the attention you intend. You can use
I owe you an apology
or
I'm really sorry I did that
and explain the action.
Avoid relying only on
I'm sorry you feel that way
when you mean to take responsibility for something you did. That wording focuses on their feeling rather than naming your action. Compare
I'm sorry I shared your message without asking

rows.text: The incident is not a problem for you, or you are reassuring them.
I appreciate it, but I'm still upset.
You accept the words while describing a remaining feeling.
You state what you want in future.
You are not ready to continue immediately.

runs.text: You do not have to say
It's okay
if it is not okay for you.
No big deal
presents the incident as relatively unimportant; choose it when that is what you mean.

turns.speaker: Cam

runs.text: Sorry I borrowed your charger without asking.

turns.en: Sorry I borrowed your charger without asking.

turns.speaker: Jules

runs.text: Thanks for apologizing. Please ask me next time.

turns.en: Thanks for apologizing. Please ask me next time.

runs.text: Okay. I will.
I'm sorry to hear that
can express concern about someone else's bad news. It need not mean you caused the event.
My grandfather died last week.

turns.speaker: Cam

runs.text: I'm so sorry for your loss.

turns.en: I'm so sorry for your loss.

runs.text: Thank you. I appreciate that.

blocks.caption: Sympathy is a different use · Jules & Cam

runs.text: For other difficult news,
I'm sorry you're having such a hard time
offers acknowledgment. Chapter 19 develops support.
Sorry?
can also ask for repetition, as in Chapter 4; that is another function of the same word.
Speak both roles when practicing alone. First use Study; then cover it and change the event or response.
You accidentally bump into a friend. Give a short apology. They are not bothered. Supply their reassuring reply.
You sent the wrong meeting time: six instead of seven. Acknowledge your mistake and correct the information.
Someone borrowed your headphones without asking. They apologize. Your role wants them to ask next time and does not want to say everything is fine. Respond.
A friend says
My dog died yesterday
. Express sympathy. The friend answers
Thank you
. Do not speak as though you caused the death.
A person speaks too quietly. Use
Sorry?
or a fuller Chapter 4 repair phrase. Explain why this is not an apology for wrongdoing.
Hide Study. Rehearse a four-turn exchange about a forgotten message, using a concrete next step and a response that fits the recipient's feelings.
Sample possibilities
Oops, sorry! — No problem.
My bad. It should say seven. I'll correct the message.
Thanks for apologizing. Please ask me next time.
I'm so sorry to hear that.
Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say it again?
You are requesting information.
Check:
Was it clear whether you were apologizing, showing sympathy or asking for repetition? Did an apology identify the action? Did the recipient have room to state an honest response?
